source: 1662 Book of Common Prayer opening sentences
rotation: Sunday-first. Morning uses the day's sentence; Evening uses the next sentence so the two offices never share one on the same day.

sentences.bcp1662: When the wicked man turneth away from his wickedness that he hath committed, and doeth that which is lawful and right, he shall save his soul alive.
sentences.bsb: But if a wicked man turns from the wickedness he has committed and does what is just and right, he will save his life.

sentences.bcp1662: I acknowledge my transgressions, and my sin is ever before me.
sentences.bsb: For I know my transgressions, and my sin is always before me.

sentences.bcp1662: Hide thy face from my sins, and blot out all mine iniquities.
sentences.bsb: Hide Your face from my sins and blot out all my iniquities.

sentences.bcp1662: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.
sentences.bsb: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.

sentences.bcp1662: Rend your heart and not your garments, and turn unto the Lord your God, for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil.
sentences.bsb: So rend your hearts and not your garments, and return to the LORD your God. For He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion. And He relents from sending disaster.

sentences.bcp1662: To the Lord our God belong mercies and forgivenesses, though we have rebelled against him, neither have we obeyed the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in his laws which he set before us.
sentences.bsb: To the Lord our God belong compassion and forgiveness, even though we have rebelled against Him and have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God to walk in His laws, which He set before us through His servants the prophets.

sentences.bcp1662: O Lord, correct me, but with judgement; not in thine anger, lest thou bring me to nothing.
sentences.bsb: Correct me, O LORD, but only with justice—not in Your anger, or You will bring me to nothing. O LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger or discipline me in Your wrath.
